newsitem.title: USA: MS Financial breaks covenants, hires advisor.
newsitem.headline: MS Financial breaks covenants, hires advisor.

text.p: MS Financial Inc said on Monday that its year-to-date loss and inability to complete a securitization caused MS Financial to violate certain covenants of its revolving credit facility.

The company said it is unable to make any more borrowings under such a facility and is negotiating for waivers or amendments to the relevant loan documents. The company said its other source of borrowing, a securitized warehouse line, cannot be used at this time.
MS Financial also said it reached an agreement to sell loans to a third party, which allows the company to continue funding contracts.
The company has retained Bear Stearns & Co Inc to provide financial advice on financing and strategic alternatives.

MS Financial is evaluating the possibility of additional loan sales, or a securitization of a portion of its installment contracts. It also said it is evaluating issuing convertible subordinated debentures, as well as a merger with or possible sale of MS Financial or its assets to another company.
The company posted on Monday a net loss of $4.0 million, or $0.38 per share, for the third quarter compared with net income of $4.3 million, or $0.40 per share, for the same period in 1995.

MS Financial, which purchases and services installment contracts on new and used cars and light duty trucks, said the loss was a result of a $6.7 million increase in loan loss reserves in September and the fact that the company did not close a securitization.
